scope: Incidence-aware follow-up; each directly consulted paper/version receives an outcome. Bibliography-only citations do not trigger recursion.

papers.title: On the Efficacy of the Peeling Decoder for the Quantum Expander Code
papers.comparison: Distinguishes stabilizer, horizontal and vertical stopping sets, citing Connolly et al.; SSF guarantees require constituent left/right expansion and delta<1/8. This does not assert a small second singular value for an expanded CSS check matrix, nor the exact stopping distance of B1.

papers.title: Finding All Small Error-Prone Substructures in LDPC Codes
papers.comparison: Classical exhaustive narrowing and branch-and-bound search is established prior art, including bit-rooted enumeration and automorphisms. Our method is a small degree-one extension certificate, not a new general enumeration method. The paper provides methods for arbitrary Tanner matrices, not an inspected exact B1 certificate. Introductory dependency/FER/codeword questions are answered later in this paper.

papers.title: Cluster Decomposition for Improved Erasure Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.comparison: Explicitly studies the [[882,24]] B1 code in Figure7 and cites the stabilizer-support stopping-set lemma. It supplies simulations and a post-peeling decomposition decoder, not an exact stopping-distance-six theorem or the source spectral inequality. The proposed generalization of VH decomposition is addressed by this paper; its speculation about a cluster-size phase transition is held as context rather than promoted to a precise conjecture.

papers.title: On the Analysis of Stopping Sets Associated with the Quantum Hypergraph Product Code
papers.comparison: Author conference page confirms the ISIT2026 title/authors. DOI full text was inaccessible; a secondary abstract describes stabilizer and horizontal/vertical stopping probabilities for ordinary HGP codes. Full theorem hypotheses and question screen remain unassessed; no zero-question or exact B1 claim.

held_context.passage: Speculation about a phase transition in cluster sizes along increasing code length.
held_context.outcome: Context held; no precise author-posed conjecture was frozen.
Dependency evaluation, FER conversion and Ramanujan–Margulis minimum-codeword questions are answered later in this paper; not newly open entries.
